column1: # stateful-op-reminder — nudges before a mutation to an external system, and stays
# out of the way otherwise. It never blocks, so every case here is `ctx` or `allow`:
# the interesting axis is whether it fired, not what exit code it chose.
# `ctx` rather than `allow` is the whole point. A reminder emits no permissionDecision,
# so on an exit-code-only harness a fired reminder and a silent pass score identically
# and no case can tell them apart.
# --- must nudge: mutations to cluster, infra and identity state ---
ctx
ctx
ctx
# --- must stay silent: the read-only siblings of each of the above ---
# Plus `kubectl delete`, which is deliberately NOT this hook's job: deletion belongs
# to destructive-guard, which asks or blocks rather than merely reminding. Pinned
# here so a future widening of this matcher shows up as two hooks firing on one
# command rather than as a silently doubled prompt.
allow
allow
allow
allow
allow
allow
allow
# --- must stay silent on the pattern as message text rather than as an invocation.
# A reminder that matches its own trigger inside a commit subject fires on the commit
# that documents it — and because it only adds context, nobody notices it is wrong.
allow
